correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and boundaries reconstructed: squarefull exponents are zero or at least two. Alternating monotonicity bounds every prime-power local factor by f_p(3) and f_p(2). Exact Euler product gives 630/pi^6. For primes p=5,...,23 exact finite products certify each log weight does not exceed the tail. Nagura and the explicit inequalities 24/(25q^2)<-log f_q(3)<1/q^2 close every p>=25; greedy subsums yield [L,1]. Four local support cases fill bands using exponents two or three, and exact rational pi bounds establish all overlaps and two strict gaps. Replayed standalone verifier prints VERIFY_OK. The finite sample is supporting evidence, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Originality supported for the restricted-domain three-component theorem: the closest known exact result is for unrestricted integers and its proof constructs interval filling with exponent-one local factors. Its theorem does not imply the topology after requiring every occurring prime exponent >=2. The new proof requires the distinct prime-cube Euler product and tail subsum estimates; the source-defining 2015 paper has no squarefull-range classification. Searches found no matching exact classification. Risk of an unlocated equivalent is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Equivalent squarefull classification may exist under other terminology or in an unlocated follow-up. The restricted-domain sigma paper was not inspected exhaustively, although its arithmetic function is distinct.
Nagura prime interval theorem is classical imported input, rather than reproved here; all other nontrivial steps are independently shown.

value.rationale: Squarefull integers are a standard multiplicatively defined class with a genuine forbidden exponent-one condition, not an arbitrary finite slice. The natural density/range-topology question for the alternating divisor function changes from two components on all integers to three on squarefull integers. The prime-cube Kakeya mechanism and exact zeta/π endpoints explain the transition. This is an exact global structural classification, not a table of small examples or a mere restatement of the unrestricted theorem.
